purpose: Determine whether the serial regime is a memory fact or a scheduler artifact, after the full sweep derived regime_decision=serial while logging evictions in which predicted < available.

conditions.note: MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2 set via /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/zz-phase0-coresidency-test.conf for this probe only.

trials.note: Establishes that multi-runner works at all on this backend; MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2 is effective.
The judge is not itself unloadable-with-others; rules out a per-model quirk.
Highest confirmed-good footprint before introducing the judge.
Q4_K_M developer co-resides with the judge.
Q4 developer at the top of the swept context range, still co-resident, both 100% GPU.
Q8_0 developer resident, judge refused despite predicted < available.
Lowering context does not help; the refusal tracks total footprint, not KV size.

effective_coresidency_budget_gib.note: Ollama withholds roughly 8-15 GiB beneath the 96 GiB GTT ceiling; its own 'available' figure overstates what it will actually grant.

findings.q8_developer_plus_judge: serial (88.4 GiB exceeds the effective budget)
findings.q4_developer_plus_judge: coresident at 79-81 GiB, developer up to 49152 ctx, both 100% GPU

regime_rationale: Not a capacity claim about the 96 GiB ceiling, which the Q4 arm disproves, but a quant tradeoff. Co-residency is reachable only by demoting the developer from Q8_0 to Q4_K_M. Measured swap cost is 8.0 s judge->developer and 13.2 s developer->judge, which is small against per-stage runtimes, so paying the swap to keep Q8_0 weights is the better trade. Revisit if swap_overhead_pct telemetry exceeds ~15%.
